edges.description: Chronic mucosal carcinogen exposure is what produces the genetically altered field this node describes. The intermediates between adduct formation and a clinically visible field are not specified here.

Acetaldehyde generated locally in saliva by oral microbiota and mucosal enzymes adds a second genotoxic exposure to the same field, which is why the joint effect with tobacco exceeds the product of the two.

Areca nut reaches this node through a named intermediate rather than an unknown one: oral submucous fibrosis is itself the premalignant lesion, and it is the step at which chewing becomes carcinoma risk. This is what distinguishes the areca route from the tobacco and ethanol routes, which act on the field directly.

nodes.description: Oral cavity SCC cells upregulate the PD-L1 immune-checkpoint ligand, which engages PD-1 on tumor-infiltrating T cells to dampen anti-tumor immunity and permit immune escape, particularly in recurrent/metastatic disease. This adaptive immune resistance is the mechanistic rationale for PD-1 checkpoint-inhibitor therapy.

Oral submucous fibrosis (OSMF) has a high rate of malignant transformation and

nodes.description: CDKN2A (encoding p16INK4a) is inactivated by deletion, mutation, or promoter hypermethylation in a majority of HPV-independent oral cavity SCC. Loss of p16 removes inhibition of CDK4/6, driving RB phosphorylation and unrestrained G1/S cell-cycle progression.

nodes.description: EGFR is overexpressed in the majority of oral cavity SCC and amplified in a subset. EGFR signaling activates RAS-MAPK and PI3K-AKT cascades that promote proliferation, survival, and invasion, providing the rationale for EGFR-targeted therapy.

nodes.description: PD-1 inhibitors (pembrolizumab, nivolumab) are approved for recurrent or metastatic head and neck SCC, including oral cavity primaries, as monotherapy or with chemotherapy.

Oral cavity SCC invades local structures (muscle, bone, perineural spaces) and metastasizes early to the cervical lymph nodes via lymphatic spread. Epithelial-mesenchymal transition and matrix remodeling underlie invasion; depth of invasion and nodal status are key prognostic determinants.

nodes.description: Metformin is under investigation as a chemopreventive ("interception") agent for oral premalignant lesions (leukoplakia, erythroplakia, oral epithelial dysplasia) — the field-cancerization precursors of oral cavity SCC — in otherwise healthy, non-diabetic high-risk individuals. By activating AMPK and indirectly suppressing PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling in the dysplastic basal epithelium, it aims to reverse dysplasia before invasive transformation. In a single-arm phase IIa trial, 12 weeks of metformin produced histological improvement in 60% of oral premalignant lesions (17% complete responses), and response correlated with reduced lesional mTOR activity (pS6). This is a prevention-setting repurposing distinct from metformin's antidiabetic use.

evidence.reference_title: Inhibition of mTOR signaling and clinical activity of metformin in oral premalignant lesions.
evidence.snippet: Here, we conducted a single-arm, open-label phase IIa clinical trial in individuals with oral premalignant lesions (OPLs) to explore the potential of metformin to target PI3K/mTOR signaling for HNSCC prevention.

nodes.description: The PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway is among the most frequently altered signaling pathways in oral cancer, activated by PIK3CA amplification/mutation (3q26) and PTEN loss. Pathway activation drives proliferation and survival downstream of EGFR and contributes to the malignant phenotype.

nodes.description: TP53 is the most frequently mutated gene in HPV-independent oral cavity SCC. Tobacco carcinogen-induced mutations inactivate p53, abolishing cell-cycle checkpoints and apoptosis in response to DNA damage and permitting clonal expansion of genetically unstable cells.
